posts.title: Carrot Pickles
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Crisp refrigerator carrot pickles with lemon, cider vinegar, mustard seed, chili, and optional ginger, green chili, and turmeric.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.264
posts.body_markdown:
Carrot Pickles are a quick refrigerator condiment built from thin carrot sticks, lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, salt, chili powder, crushed mustard seeds, and optional ginger, green chili, and turmeric.

This pickle is assembled entirely in a jar rather than cooked. The carrots are cut into long thin sticks so the seasoning can coat a large surface area while the vegetables stay crisp.

After mixing, the jar rests in the refrigerator for at least two hours and is shaken from time to time. The source keeps the method deliberately simple and notes that the pickles hold for at least a week.

## Ingredients
- 3 carrots, cut into 2 1/2-inch (6-cm) long thin sticks
- 1/2 teaspoon lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon chili powder, or to taste
- 1 teaspoon yellow mustard seeds, crushed
- 2 slices fresh ginger, optional
- 2 fresh green chilies, slit at the end, optional
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, optional
- If only lemon juice or vinegar is available, use 2 1/2 tablespoons of that one ingredient

## Method
Combine all ingredients in a jar with a lid and shake well. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving, shaking the jar from time to time. Keep refrigerated for at least 1 week. Makes 2–2 1/2 cups.

posts.title: Green Mangoes with Salt & Cayenne
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Green Mangoes with Salt & Cayenne | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A raw green-mango condiment seasoned simply with salt and cayenne, ready to serve as soon as the fruit is diced and mixed.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.264
posts.body_markdown:
Green Mangoes with Salt & Cayenne is a three-ingredient condiment that highlights the sharp, firm character of unripe mango.

The mango is diced rather than cooked, then seasoned only with salt and cayenne. Because there is no resting or heating stage, the quality of the raw mango determines the final texture.

The source also explains how to cut around the large flat mango seed before dicing the flesh. Once cut and seasoned, the condiment is ready to serve immediately.

## Ingredients
- 2 raw green mangoes, diced
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste

## Method
Slice each mango on either side of the large central seed, trim away the remaining flesh around the seed, discard the seed, and dice the mango. Combine the diced green mango, salt, and cayenne in a bowl and serve. Makes 1 1/2–2 cups.

posts.title: Homemade Yogurt
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A two-ingredient homemade yogurt cultured from warm whole milk and a spoonful of yogurt, then left in a warm place for 8–12 hours.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.266
posts.body_markdown:
Homemade Yogurt uses only whole milk and a small amount of room-temperature yogurt as the starter culture.

The milk is heated until it foams, then cooled to lukewarm before the starter is whisked in. The source gives about 100°F (38°C) as a practical temperature cue before inoculating the milk.

The covered bowl then sits undisturbed in a warm, draft-free place for 8–12 hours. A portion of the finished yogurt can be reserved to start the next batch.

## Ingredients
- 4 cups organic whole milk
- 2 heaping tablespoons organic yogurt, at room temperature

## Method
Heat the milk in a pot over medium heat until it foams up. Turn off the heat and let it cool until lukewarm, about 100°F (38°C). Pour into a very clean or sterilized bowl and whisk in the room-temperature yogurt. Cover and leave in a warm, draft-free place for 8–12 hours before using. Reserve some yogurt as starter for the next batch if desired. Makes 4 cups.

posts.title: Cumin Raita
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A simple cumin raita made from plain yogurt and coarsely crushed cumin, with cayenne and fresh herbs as the finishing garnish.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.267
posts.body_markdown:
Cumin Raita is a minimal yogurt condiment seasoned with coarsely crushed cumin and optional salt, then finished with cayenne and fresh herbs.

The cumin is intentionally kept coarse rather than ground to a fine powder. That gives the raita visible flecks and a more distinct cumin texture.

This raita requires no cooking. Once the yogurt, cumin, and salt are mixed, the cayenne and mint or cilantro are added as the final garnish.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup plain yogurt
- 1/4 teaspoon whole cumin seeds, crushed
- 1/4 teaspoon salt, optional
- Pinch of cayenne pepper, for garnish
- 1 sprig fresh mint or cilantro leaves, for garnish

## Method
Combine the yogurt, crushed cumin, and optional salt in a bowl. Sprinkle with cayenne and garnish with fresh mint or cilantro. To crush the cumin, keep it coarse rather than powdering it. Makes 1 cup.

posts.title: Cucumber Raita
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A cool cucumber raita in which grated cucumber is salted, drained, and squeezed before being folded into yogurt and garnished.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.267
posts.body_markdown:
Cucumber Raita starts by lightly salting grated cucumber and draining it before the cucumber is mixed into yogurt.

The half-hour draining step is important because it removes excess water that would otherwise thin the finished raita. The cucumber is squeezed again before it reaches the yogurt.

Once mixed, the raita is finished with a pinch of cayenne and fresh cilantro. The result stays cool and spoonable rather than watery.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 teaspoon salt, for the cucumber
- 1/2 cucumber, grated
- 1 1/2 cups plain yogurt
- 1/4 teaspoon salt, for the mixture, optional
- Pinch of cayenne pepper, for garnish
- 1 sprig fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

## Method
Lightly salt the grated cucumber and leave it in a sieve to drain for 30 minutes. Squeeze out the excess water. Combine the drained cucumber with the yogurt and optional additional salt. Sprinkle with cayenne, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 1 3/4 cups.

posts.title: Tomato Raisin Raita
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A sweet-and-sour raita of diced tomatoes, yogurt, and briefly soaked raisins, finished with cumin and fresh cilantro.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.268
posts.body_markdown:
Tomato Raisin Raita combines fresh diced tomato with plain yogurt and softened raisins for a clear sweet-and-sour contrast.

The raisins are soaked in water for five minutes before they are stirred into the yogurt. That short soak plumps them without changing the fresh texture of the tomatoes.

Ground cumin and cilantro are used only as garnish, so the base remains focused on yogurt, tomato, and raisins.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 cup raisins
- 2 cups plain yogurt
- 1/2 cup tomatoes, diced
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, for garnish
- 1 sprig fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish
- Optional source variation: an additional 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro

## Method
Soak the raisins in a small bowl of water for 5 minutes. Combine the yogurt and tomatoes in a serving bowl. Drain the raisins and stir them into the yogurt mixture. Sprinkle with ground cumin, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 2 3/4 cups.

posts.title: Spinach Raita
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A quick spinach raita with one-minute blanched spinach, plain yogurt, toasted cumin, salt, and cayenne.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.268
posts.body_markdown:
Spinach Raita combines briefly blanched spinach with yogurt, salt, toasted ground cumin, and cayenne.

The spinach is cooked for only one minute in boiling water. It is then drained and squeezed thoroughly so the yogurt stays thick rather than becoming diluted.

All of the ingredients are mixed together after the spinach has been prepared, making this a short recipe with one essential texture-control step.

## Ingredients
- 3 cups spinach, chopped
- 2 cups plain yogurt
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin seeds, toasted and ground
- Cayenne pepper to taste

## Method
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the chopped spinach and blanch for 1 minute. Drain and squeeze out the excess water. Combine the spinach, yogurt, salt, toasted ground cumin, and cayenne in a bowl and mix well. Makes 2 3/4 cups.

posts.title: Coconut & Banana Raita
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A banana-yogurt raita finished with a quick mustard-seed and coconut tempering, then chilled for one hour before serving.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.269
posts.body_markdown:
Coconut & Banana Raita pairs sliced banana with yogurt, then adds a separate tempering of mustard seeds and grated coconut.

The mustard seeds are heated in olive oil until they pop, after which the coconut and a small spoonful of yogurt are stirred through the pan for only a few seconds.

That warm coconut mixture is folded into the cold banana-yogurt base. The finished raita is garnished with cilantro and chilled for one hour before serving.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/4 cups plain yogurt
- 1 cup bananas, sliced
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 teaspoon black mustard seeds
- 2 1/2 tablespoons coconut, grated
- 1 1/2 tablespoons plain yogurt
- 1 teaspoon fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Combine 1 1/4 cups yogurt with the bananas and salt and set aside. Heat the olive oil in a small frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the coconut and stir for a few seconds, then add 1 1/2 tablespoons yogurt and stir for a few more seconds. Mix this warm coconut mixture into the banana-yogurt bowl. Garnish with cilantro, cover, and refrigerate for 1 hour before serving. Makes about 3 cups.

posts.title: Almond Milk
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Fresh almond milk made by soaking and peeling almonds, blending them with water, and straining through cheesecloth before optional sweetening.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.272
posts.body_markdown:
Almond Milk begins with an overnight soak, followed by skinning, blending, and straining the almonds into a fresh non-dairy drink.

After soaking, boiling water is poured over the almonds to loosen the skins. The peeled almonds are blended very smooth before fresh water is added and the mixture is blended again.

Cheesecloth separates the milk from the remaining almond solids. Maple syrup or honey is optional, and the leftover almond mixture can be saved for other recipes.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup almonds
- 2 cups purified water, for soaking
- 3 cups purified water, for blending
- Maple syrup to taste, or honey, optional

## Method
Soak the almonds in 2 cups purified water overnight. Drain. Pour boiling water over the almonds, let them cool slightly, and squeeze off the skins. Blend the peeled almonds until very smooth. Add 3 cups purified water and blend for 3 minutes. Strain through cheesecloth into a pitcher, squeezing out as much liquid as possible. Sweeten with maple syrup or honey if desired. Makes 3 cups.

posts.title: Spicy Almond Milk
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A blended almond-milk drink with ginger, poppy seed, anise, black pepper, and maple syrup or honey.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.273
posts.body_markdown:
Spicy Almond Milk blends a fresh ginger paste with poppy seeds, anise, black pepper, maple syrup, almond milk, and water.

The ginger is puréed first so it disperses evenly through the drink. The spices and sweetener are then blended in before the liquids are added in stages.

Because the recipe is fully blended rather than steeped or strained, the ground poppy seeds remain in the finished drink and contribute to its texture.

## Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons fresh ginger, roughly chopped
- 4 teaspoons poppy seeds
- 1 teaspoon ground anise
- 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 4 tablespoons maple syrup or honey, or to taste
- 1/2 cup water
- 2 cups Almond Milk
- 2 cups water

## Method
Purée the ginger in a blender or food processor until it becomes a paste. Add the poppy seeds, anise, black pepper, and maple syrup or honey and blend again. Add 1/2 cup water and blend. Add the almond milk and remaining 2 cups water and continue blending until well mixed. Pour into a pitcher and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Cinnamon & Sweet Warm Almond Milk
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Cinnamon & Sweet Warm Almond Milk | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A warm almond-milk drink gently infused with a cinnamon stick and sweetened with honey after the pan comes off the heat.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.274
posts.body_markdown:
Cinnamon & Sweet Warm Almond Milk gently warms prepared almond milk with a whole cinnamon stick and finishes it with honey.

The key is to heat the drink only until warmed through rather than boiling it. The cinnamon flavors the milk during warming and can continue to infuse after the pan leaves the heat.

Honey is added only after the saucepan is removed from the stove. The drink can then be served directly in mugs or transferred to a teapot.

## Ingredients
- 3 1/2 cups Almond Milk
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 1 tablespoon honey

## Method
Combine the almond milk and cinnamon stick in a large saucepan over medium heat and warm gently. As soon as the mixture is heated through, remove it from the heat. Stir in the honey and serve. Makes 3 servings.

posts.title: The Cold Feet Cure: Almond Milk with Crushed Pistachios & Rose Water
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: The Cold Feet Cure: Almond Milk with Crushed Pistachios & Rose Water | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A no-cook almond-milk drink with crushed pistachios, cardamom, nutmeg, rose water, optional saffron, and sweetener to taste.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.274
posts.body_markdown:
The Cold Feet Cure is a no-cook almond-milk drink flavored with crushed pistachios, cardamom, nutmeg, rose water, sweetener, and optional saffron.

Everything is mixed directly in a pitcher, so the preparation depends on balancing the aromatic ingredients rather than on heat or steeping.

The crushed pistachios remain in the drink for texture, while cardamom, nutmeg, rose water, and optional saffron provide the main fragrance.

## Ingredients
- 4 cups Almond Milk
- 2 tablespoons unsalted pistachios, crushed
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 1/8 teaspoon nutmeg
- Sweetener to taste
- A few drops rose water
- A few strands saffron, optional

## Method
Combine the almond milk, pistachios, cardamom, nutmeg, sweetener, rose water, and optional saffron in a pitcher. Mix well and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Nice & Nutty Brown Rice Milk
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Nice & Nutty Brown Rice Milk | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A homemade brown-rice milk made by simmering short-grain rice for 1 1/2 hours, then blending it smooth with optional flavor variations.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.275
posts.body_markdown:
Nice & Nutty Brown Rice Milk cooks short-grain brown rice slowly in a large volume of water before blending the cooked mixture smooth.

The rice simmers covered for 1 1/2 hours, giving the grain enough time to soften fully before puréeing. Salt is the only seasoning in the base version.

The source also gives three optional variations: dark chocolate, cinnamon with maple syrup, or flax seeds. The finished rice milk can be refrigerated for up to seven days.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup short-grain organic brown rice, uncooked
- 8 cups water
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- Variation 1: melted 70% cocoa-mass dark chocolate
- Variation 2: ground cinnamon to taste and maple syrup
- Variation 3: 1–2 tablespoons flax seeds

## Method
Combine the rice, water, and salt in a large pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 1 1/2 hours. Remove from the heat and purée in a blender or food processor until smooth. Add any optional variation if desired. Refrigerate for up to 7 days. Makes about 6 cups.

posts.title: The Salty Lassi
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A light salty lassi made by whisking yogurt with crushed cumin, salt, and water until smooth.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.276
posts.body_markdown:
The Salty Lassi is a straightforward yogurt drink seasoned with crushed cumin and salt, then diluted with water until smooth.

There is no heating or resting stage. The entire recipe is whisked together directly in a pitcher, which keeps the preparation quick.

The proportion of three cups water to one cup yogurt makes this much lighter than a spoonable raita while preserving the tang of the yogurt and the aroma of cumin.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup plain yogurt
- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds, crushed
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 3 cups water

## Method
Combine the yogurt, crushed cumin, salt, and water in a pitcher. Whisk until completely smooth and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: The Bonny Sweet Lassi
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A sweet lassi of yogurt, cardamom, sweetener, and water, with optional fresh ginger for a brighter finish.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.276
posts.body_markdown:
The Bonny Sweet Lassi is a sweet yogurt drink flavored with cardamom and optional fresh ginger.

Like the salty version, it is prepared entirely in a pitcher with no cooking. Yogurt, sweetener, spice, and water are simply whisked until smooth.

The optional grated ginger adds a sharper note against the sweetness, while cardamom supplies the main aroma.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup plain yogurt
- 2 tablespoons sweetener
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 3 cups water
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated, optional

## Method
Combine the yogurt, sweetener, cardamom, water, and optional grated ginger in a pitcher. Whisk until smooth and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Pineapple & Coconut Cocktail
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A tropical pineapple-and-coconut drink brightened with lime and finished with fresh strawberry and mint garnishes.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.277
posts.body_markdown:
Pineapple & Coconut Cocktail combines pineapple juice and coconut milk with lime and optional maple syrup for a simple tropical drink.

The liquid ingredients are mixed directly in a pitcher, so the recipe comes together without a blender or cooking.

Each glass is finished with a strawberry set on the rim and a mint leaf. Those garnishes add fresh color and aroma to an otherwise very simple drink.

## Ingredients
- 3 cups pineapple juice
- 1 cup coconut milk
- 2 teaspoons maple syrup, optional
- 1/2 teaspoon lime juice
- 4 strawberries, for garnish
- 4 fresh mint leaves, for garnish

## Method
Combine the pineapple juice, coconut milk, optional maple syrup, and lime juice in a pitcher and mix well. Divide among 4 glasses. Slit the strawberries so they can sit on the rims and place one strawberry and one mint leaf on each glass. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Ginger Mint Cocktail
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A strained ginger-and-mint drink blended with lime, water, and maple syrup or honey, then finished with fresh mint.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.277
posts.body_markdown:
Ginger Mint Cocktail blends fresh ginger and mint with lime juice, maple syrup or honey, and water before the drink is strained.

The ginger is puréed first, followed by the mint, so both fresh ingredients are fully broken down before the liquid ingredients are added.

Cheesecloth removes the fibrous solids after blending. The strained drink is then poured into glasses and finished with fresh mint leaves.

## Ingredients
- 4 teaspoons fresh ginger, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, roughly chopped
- 1/4 cup lime juice
- 4 teaspoons maple syrup or honey
- 4 cups water
- 4 fresh mint leaves, for garnish

## Method
Purée the ginger in a blender or food processor until it becomes a paste. Add the mint and purée again. Add the lime juice, maple syrup or honey, and water and blend. Strain through cheesecloth, pour into glasses, and garnish with fresh mint leaves. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Rejuvelac
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A week-long fermented beverage of sprouted rye and wheat berries, with beet added before a final 48-hour fermentation and straining.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.278
posts.body_markdown:
Rejuvelac is a multi-day fermented beverage made from sprouted rye and wheat berries with fresh beet pieces added during the fermentation stage.

The process begins by dividing soaked grains among six wide-mouth jars, rinsing them twice daily, and draining the jars at an angle until long, tangled sprouts develop.

Once sprouted, the grains are rinsed, returned to clean jars with beet pieces and lukewarm water, then fermented for 48 hours. The finished liquid is strained and refrigerated.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup rye berries
- 1/2 cup hard wheat berries
- 1 1/2 cups soft wheat berries
- 3 medium beets
- Water as needed for soaking, rinsing, and filling 6 jars
- Equipment: 6 wide-mouth 1–2 qt (1–2 l) jars with lids
- Equipment: mesh screen squares and thick elastic bands
- Equipment: dish rack and cheesecloth

## Method
Day 1 morning: mix the rye and wheat berries and divide evenly among 6 jars, keeping each jar no more than one-third full. Fill with water, stir, cover the mouths with mesh secured by elastic bands, and leave in indirect sunlight for 8–16 hours. Day 1 evening: drain through the mesh and rinse the grains 3 times with cold water. Set the jars mouth-down at about a 45-degree angle to drain and aerate. Day 2 morning and evening: repeat the rinse-and-drain process. Days 3–5: continue rinsing morning and evening until the grains have long, tangled sprouts about 1/3–3/4 inch (1–2 cm). On day 4 or 5, remove the sprouts, rinse them 3 times, discard any unsprouted grains, and return equal portions to the jars. Peel and quarter the beets and place 2 pieces in each jar. Fill with lukewarm water, secure the mesh, and leave in indirect sunlight for 48 hours. Around day 6 or 7, when the liquid tastes slightly lemony, strain through cheesecloth into clean jars. If it is not ready after 48 hours, ferment up to another 12 hours. Seal and refrigerate. Makes about 1 gallon (4 liters).

posts.title: Rooibos Chai
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A spiced rooibos chai simmered with cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, peppercorns, optional orange peel and ginger, then steeped before serving.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.281
posts.body_markdown:
Rooibos Chai simmers rooibos with cinnamon, cardamom, peppercorns, cloves, optional orange peel, optional ginger, milk or water, and additional water.

The ingredients first come to a boil together, then simmer for five minutes. The tea is poured into a teapot afterward rather than served immediately.

A final 3–8 minute steep deepens the rooibos and spice flavor. The source also explains how to dry orange peel if using that optional ingredient.

## Ingredients
- 2–3 plain rooibos tea bags, or 2 heaping teaspoons loose rooibos
- 1 cinnamon stick, or 2–3 broken pieces cinnamon bark
- 2–3 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 2–4 whole peppercorns
- 1 tablespoon dried orange peel, chopped, optional
- 2–3 cloves
- 1–2 slices fresh ginger, optional
- 1 cup milk or water
- 2 cups water

## Method
Combine all ingredients in a large pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Pour into a teapot and let steep for 3–8 minutes before serving. Makes 3 servings. To dry orange peel at home, the source suggests leaving chopped washed peel covered in the sun for a few days or baking it at 200°F (95°C) for 15–20 minutes.

posts.title: Masala Chai Mix
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A toasted chai spice blend of clove, black pepper, cardamom, nutmeg, cinnamon, and ginger, ground and stored for adding to tea.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.282
posts.body_markdown:
Masala Chai Mix is a dry blend of cloves, black pepper, cardamom, nutmeg, cinnamon, and ginger designed to be added to brewed tea.

The whole and ground spices are toasted together in a dry frying pan for 3–4 minutes. Constant stirring keeps the spices aromatic without scorching them.

After cooling briefly, the toasted mixture is ground in batches and combined again before storage. The source recommends starting with 1/8–1/4 teaspoon per cup of tea.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon cloves
- 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 1 teaspoon cardamom seeds
- 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg, grated
- One 2-inch (5-cm) piece cinnamon bark, or 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
- 1 teaspoon ground ginger

## Method
Combine all ingredients in a dry frying pan over medium heat and toast for 3–4 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from the heat. Grind the toasted spices in batches in a spice or coffee grinder, then mix the batches together and store in an airtight container. Use about 1/8–1/4 teaspoon per cup of tea, adjusting to taste. Makes about 1/4 cup.

posts.title: Milky Masala Chai
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A classic milky masala chai simmered with black tea and the cookbook’s toasted spice blend, then strained and optionally sweetened.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.282
posts.body_markdown:
Milky Masala Chai combines water, milk, the prepared Masala Chai Mix, black tea, and optional sweetener in one pot.

The mixture is brought to a boil while being stirred so the milk does not catch on the bottom of the pan. As soon as it boils, the heat is reduced.

Five minutes of simmering is enough to infuse the tea and spices. The chai is then strained, sweetened if desired, and served.

## Ingredients
- 3 cups water
- 1 cup milk or soy milk
- 1/2–3/4 teaspoon Masala Chai Mix
- 1–2 teaspoons loose-leaf black tea, or 1–2 tea bags
- Sweetener to taste, optional

## Method
Combine the water, milk, Masala Chai Mix, and black tea in a large pot over high heat. Bring to a boil, stirring so the milk does not burn. Reduce the heat immediately and simmer for 5 minutes. Strain, add sweetener if desired, and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Tea Fit for a Yogi
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Tea Fit for a Yogi | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A coarse spiced tea blend of cinnamon, fenugreek, cardamom, clove, peppercorn, fennel, and fresh ginger for steeping in hot water.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.283
posts.body_markdown:
Tea Fit for a Yogi is a dry herbal-spice mixture of cinnamon, fenugreek, cardamom, cloves, peppercorns, fennel, and fresh ginger.

The whole dry spices are first lightly crushed in a paper bag rather than ground to powder. That keeps the finished blend coarse enough for steeping.

The crushed spices are mixed with chopped fresh ginger and stored airtight. To serve, a small amount of the blend is steeped in a pot of hot water to the desired strength.

## Ingredients
- 6 small pieces cinnamon bark
- 1 teaspoon whole fenugreek seeds
- 1 teaspoon cardamom pods
- 1 teaspoon cloves
- 1 teaspoon whole peppercorns
- 2 teaspoons fennel seeds
- 2 teaspoons fresh ginger, chopped

## Method
Place all ingredients except the ginger in a brown paper bag and crush them with a rolling pin or by gently tapping with a hammer. Transfer to a large bowl, add the chopped ginger, and mix. Use 1–2 teaspoons of the mixture per pot of hot water and steep to taste. Store the remaining tea mixture in an airtight container. Makes 4–5 tablespoons.

posts.title: Lemongrass, Mint & Ginger Tea
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A large-batch tea simmered with fresh mint, lemongrass, ginger, cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon, then strained before serving.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.283
posts.body_markdown:
Lemongrass, Mint & Ginger Tea is a large-pot infusion of fresh mint, lemongrass, ginger, cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon.

All of the ingredients go into the pot together with water. The tea is brought to a boil first and then simmered so the herbs and whole spices can infuse gradually.

The simmer can run from five to ten minutes depending on the desired strength. The tea is strained before serving and makes a generous batch.

## Ingredients
- 1 bunch fresh mint leaves, chopped
- 2 sticks lemongrass
- 4 ginger tea bags, or 3 tablespoons fresh ginger, chopped
- 5 cloves
- 5 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 4–5 pieces broken cinnamon bark
- 8–10 cups water

## Method
Combine all ingredients in a large pot over high heat. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5–10 minutes depending on the strength you prefer. Strain before serving. Makes 8–10 servings.

posts.title: Daikon Tea
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A minimalist daikon tea made by simmering chopped daikon in water for 15–20 minutes and straining before serving.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.284
posts.body_markdown:
Daikon Tea is one of the simplest beverages in the cookbook, made only from roughly chopped daikon and hot water.

The daikon and water are brought to a boil together, then the heat is lowered so the root can simmer gently.

After 15–20 minutes, the tea is removed from the heat and strained. No sweetener, spice, or garnish is added in the source recipe.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 daikon, roughly chopped
- 4 cups hot water

## Method
Combine the chopped daikon and hot water in a large pot over high heat. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 15–20 minutes. Remove from the heat, strain, and serve. Makes 3–4 cups.

posts.title: Dandelion Tea
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A plain dandelion tea made from flowers, leaves, and stems simmered in water for 30 minutes, then strained.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.284
posts.body_markdown:
Dandelion Tea uses the flower, leaves, and stems of fresh dandelions rather than only one part of the plant.

The dandelions are combined with water in a large pot, brought to a boil, and then simmered for a full 30 minutes.

Once the long simmer is complete, the tea is simply strained and served. The source includes no sweetener or additional seasoning.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups dandelions, including flowers, leaves, and stems
- 4–6 cups water

## Method
Combine the dandelions and water in a large pot over high heat. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 30 minutes. Remove from the heat, strain, and serve. Makes 3–5 cups.
